Recommended for – Guitarists seeking the classic sound of Germanium or Silicon Fuzz Face, with BIAS control. The Foxey Face by Collateral has its roots in the legendary Fuzz Face pedals, immortalized by Jimi Hendrix, David Gilmour, Eric Johnson, Bonamassa, and many other guitarists. Despite its seemingly simple circuit and operation, this type of circuit requires patience and many tests in selecting ideal transistor pairs. We have a large quantity and variety of classic transistors in stock (such as AC128, OC72, BC108, BC109), as well as numerous other models, from Japanese or Soviet origin, that bring wonderful tones with very low noise levels. The germanium version features an onboard voltage inverter, allowing the pedal to be powered by standard Boss power supplies. Internally, the Foxey Face features an input control, which limits how much of your guitar signal or effects chain signal reaches the circuit – serving for fine-tuning of the tone – ranging from singing and rich sustain to the famous “glass tone” when reducing the instrument’s volume. Externally, in addition to the traditional Level and Fuzz controls, we have the Bias control, which compensates for temperature changes in the germanium transistors, offering a wide range of tones and textures, with sounds closer to an overdrive or even a more “gated” fuzz, full of velcro-like decay in the sound. - **Archive parent:** P016 Foxey Face
- **Catalog identity:** P016 Foxey Face Fuzz
- **Builder:** Collateral FX
- **Catalog type:** Fuzz
- **Identity:** Collateral FX Foxey Face, a Fuzz Face-family fuzz with selectable germanium or silicon transistor sets and external Bias.

Collateral FX describes Foxey Face as a Fuzz Face-derived design requiring careful transistor-pair selection. The builder offers germanium and silicon versions and documents examples of AC128, OC72, BC108, and BC109 devices among its available transistor families. [1]

The manufacturer notes that colors and details can vary by production batch. No complete factory colorway sequence was established. [1]

- Input control, internal.
- Level.
- Fuzz.
- Bias.
- Selectable germanium or silicon transistor versions.
- 9V operation.
- 11 x 6 x 4 cm enclosure. [1]

The germanium version includes an onboard voltage inverter so it can use standard Boss-style power supplies. [1]

The primary documented variant is the transistor-material choice: germanium or silicon. The archive keeps those as factory options rather than inventing numbered revisions.

Documented transistor families include **AC128, OC72, BC108, and BC109**, among other Japanese and Soviet devices. The exact installed pair varies by build and selected version. [1]

No exact diode specification was published.

The internal Input control limits how much signal reaches the fuzz circuit. External Bias compensates for temperature changes in germanium versions and can move the response from overdrive-like saturation toward more gated, Velcro-style decay. [1]
